subject: Fix Windows/Git-Bash curl-stub test harness (6 shell-adapter hook tests)
description:
Six pre-existing test failures on Windows/Git-Bash, all rooted in the curl-stub mechanism not being honored cross-platform. jq is now installed (1.8.1 at C:\Users\yuepr\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WinGet\Links\jq.exe) which fixed cursor-session-normalizer + hook-policy-parity, but these 6 remain:
  classify-hook-automode, classify-hook-relay, codex-hooks, cursor-classify-relay, cursor-e2e-integration (relay portion), judge-hook-nudge.

ROOT CAUSE (diagnosed): the tests write a stub `curl` bash script to e.g. TMP/bin/curl via fs.writeFileSync(..., {mode:0o755}) and prepend that dir to PATH, then spawn the shell hook (e.g. hooks/classify.sh runs `curl -s --max-time 2 -XPOST localhost:$PORT/classify ...`). The hook is expected to invoke the STUB curl (which records request args to curl-args.txt / writes a canned daemon response to stub-curl/last-body.json). On Git-Bash/Windows the 0o755 exec bit set by Node does NOT make the file executable in MSYS2's permission model, so bash skips the stub and runs the REAL /mingw64/bin/curl instead — the capture file is never created (test crashes ENOENT reading curl-args.txt / last-body.json: codex-hooks.test.js:56, cursor-classify-relay.test.js:72) and no canned response is relayed (classify-hook-* "model routing from stub"/"heartbeat from stub" fail; judge-hook-nudge nudge-text assertions fail).

TASK:
1. Confirm the diagnosis on this machine: reproduce one failure (e.g. `PATH=/c/Users/yuepr/AppData/Local/Microsoft/WinGet/Links:$PATH node test/codex-hooks.test.js`) and verify the stub curl isn't being executed (e.g. `type curl` inside the spawned env, or check whether the stub runs). Note: ALWAYS run with the jq Links dir on PATH.
2. Find the common pattern (each test inlines its own stub; there may be shared structure). Implement a cross-platform fix so the stub curl IS honored under Git-Bash/Windows AND still works on POSIX/CI. Likely options (pick the most robust, minimal, and portable — do NOT change production hook behavior):
   - Make the stub reliably executable on MSYS2 (e.g. also emit a `curl.exe`/`curl.bat` shim, or mark exec via an approach Git-Bash honors, or name/launch it so bash's shebang handling runs it), OR
   - Have the stub be a real executable Git-Bash will exec regardless of the Node mode bit.
   The fix should live in the test harness (test files / a shared test helper), NOT in the production hooks (hooks/classify.sh etc. must keep calling plain `curl`). If you find a genuine production portability bug in a hook, STOP and record_decision instead of changing it.
3. Make ALL of these green WITHOUT regressing others: codex-hooks, cursor-classify-relay, classify-hook-automode, classify-hook-relay, cursor-e2e-integration, judge-hook-nudge (and keep cursor-session-normalizer + hook-policy-parity passing).
4. Run the FULL suite at the end and report the tally; target 177/177 (or explain any genuine residual). Document any new environmental dependency.

Forks off main (flat attempt→main flow; main HEAD da2e090 already has the ws-registry merge). Read the actual test files first.
